summary: @servicetitan/data-query 41.3.3 preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute bundled obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from the oven-sh GitHub releases (or reuses a locally installed `bun`), extracts and chmod +x's it, then invokes it against a bundled 727,680-byte file `math_init.js` at the tarball root. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated (string-array rotation via `WV8StW` over a large mixed array `n7gIxM`, hex-mangled identifiers), is not referenced by the library's `dist/index.js`, and is not part of the public API. The package's declared purpose is a Kendo/OData filter/sort utility, which has no relation to Bun or a large opaque JS payload. The tarball's `files` field lists only `dist` and `src`, yet `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are shipped at the tarball root outside that declared set. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern (fetching Bun specifically to execute a sibling obfuscated blob) bypasses Node-based install-time scanners and causes attacker-controlled code to run on the installer's host on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
